events.title: The healing of the Western Schism
events.shortBlurb: With the consecration of Oddo Colonna as bishop, the Council of Constance sealed the end of the forty-year schism that had rent Latin Christendom…
body: For nearly forty years, since 1378, the Latin Church had been torn among rival claimants to the papacy, until at times three men wore the tiara and Christendom scarcely knew whom to obey. The Council of Constance, opened on 5 November 1414, set itself to end the scandal: it deposed John XXIII and Benedict XIII and received the freely-given resignation of the Roman claimant Gregory XII.

On 11 November 1417 the cardinals and the deputies of the five nations, meeting in conclave, unanimously elected Oddo Colonna, who took the name Martin V in honor of St. Martin of Tours, whose feast fell that day. Being then only a subdeacon, he was ordained deacon on the 12th, priest on the 13th, and consecrated bishop on 14 November 1417 at Constance; he was crowned pope on the 21st.

Recognized by the Church as a whole, Martin V brought the schism to an end and set about restoring the papacy and the Papal States. He soon condemned the conciliarist claim that a general council stands above the pope, forbidding appeal from the pope's judgment in matters of faith, and the long wound of Avignon and the three obediences was at last closed.
